guidance.opening: Autumn light slants through a dusty window onto a landlord's desk: lease folders, a brass inkwell, the faint smell of floor wax and pipe tobacco. Steven Knott looks up from a ledger, taps a pencil once against the blotter, and studies the visitor without yet offering a chair. "Who are you, and what sort of work do you do?" A name and an occupation idea are enough to begin; one or two questions may follow, then a complete draft will be proposed for review.
guidance.advice: 1920s Boston, autumn 1920. Useful listed occupations for a daylight inquiry into a landlord's problem house include Journalist, Private Investigator, Lawyer, Librarian, Professor, Police Detective, Police Officer, Doctor of Medicine, Antiquarian, Author, Parapsychologist, Dilettante, and Clergy; others on the list can work if the player prefers. Useful training: Library Use, History, Law, Credit Rating, Fast Talk or Persuade, Spot Hidden, Listen, Psychology; Latin or Italian can help with records and former tenants later. Era kit: notebook, fountain pen, street clothes, hat, modest cash—do not invent dollar amounts or start with house keys. Public involvement can be a referral, a newspaper contact, or simply answering a landlord's call; optional ties (Boston family, a friend in the press, curiosity about rumors) are player ideas, not authored facts. Do not decide identity, accept a hire, or hand over items. Preserve uncertainty: neighbors rumble about the Corbitt House and a Macario disaster; nothing is proven yet.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Knott's Office being asked who they are and what work they do. Identity has not been finalized and no commission, keys, or payment have been taken. Continue the meeting there to finish a character draft for review.
